pageCache.pageTitle: Ethos, Values and Mission | Pardes House Primary School
pageCache.text:
Ethos and Values
Pardes House is aligned with the Union of Orthodox Hebrew Congregations of the United Kingdom. We derive our ethos and values from the timeless values and teachings of the Torah, as transmitted through orthodox Jewish tradition.
Our pupils are expected to abide by these values, which are emphasised in the school’s ‘Magna Carta of Rights and Responsibilities’ and in daily practise. Our Va’ad HaChinuch (Rabbinic board) interpret and rule on all matters relating to the applicability of these values and teachings. The Governing Body and Senior Leadership Team aim to follow the direction of the Va’ad HaChinuch in all matters.
Mission
The mission of the school is to synthesise the religious requirements of the Va’ad HaChinuch with the highest possible standards as set out by the National Curriculum. In providing a high quality Jewish and secular educational experience, we prepare our pupils for their academic and personal development through secondary school and beyond and ensure they are equipped to successfully live a strict Torah-observant life and excel in their lives in the world. Our pupils are taught to value truth, honesty, respect for everyone, including the country they live in and its history, a lifelong love of learning and to develop great self-discipline.
All of this takes place in a safe, caring, healthy and well-structured learning environment, while promoting high standards of achievement and behaviour for all. Alongside this is our aim to build pupils’ resilience by teaching them to value truth, honesty, respect for everyone and develop a lifelong love of learning. Further, we believe it is our civic (as well as legal) duty to prevent radicalisation by promoting Fundamental British Values in the curriculum and elsewhere in school life.
As part of our mission and through a range of experiences, we commit to:
Making every second count!

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Pardes House | Pardes House Primary School
pageCache.text:
Providing solid foundations – Creating tools for growth – Building confidence for the future
Welcome to our school!
Pardes House is an over-subscribed, single-sex, voluntary aided Orthodox Jewish boys’ primary school, with almost 360 pupils. It is also the only such primary school in the London Borough of Barnet. The school, located in Finchley, North West London is now over 70 years old, opening on its current site in 1978 and became Voluntary-Aided in 2001. The school’s prime catchment is the Jewish communities of North West London and sometimes beyond, with the majority of pupils joining the school from the independent nursery on the same site.
A significant proportion of the day is dedicated to the Jewish Studies curriculum, which is taught alongside the National Curriculum. The school day is from 8.40am – 4.15pm. On Wednesdays, Years 4 – 6 attend an additional Jewish Studies session from 4.15 – 5.00pm. Extended services are provided through various clubs both before and after school.
The school holds eco-schools status and the Gold award for sustainable travel. Pardes House is also a partner of UK Parliament Week, a prem-aware school, the recipient of an award from the Speaker of the House of Commons and has been a winner of the Barnet schools British Values Project award.

Our doors are always open and we welcome our parents into our school as it is to us that they entrust their boys.
The sections below show all the ways that we interact with our parent body, both in school and out, throughout the school year.
Communication
Parents have a very important role to play in our school. We are proud at what we believe are pro-active forms of communication between school and home and vice-versa. Parents are always welcome to contact the school with any questions, concerns or requests and the school will be pro-active to contact the parents in the same way. Please click here to go to the page with all the ways we communicate with parents and information for parents on keeping their children safe online.
School opening hours
The school day for all pupils is from 8.40am – 4.15pm. Years 4, 5 and 6 have an extended school day on Wednesday, with an extra Religious Studies lesson, finishing at 5.00pm. Friday finishing times vary during the school year, dependent on what time the Sabbath commences. These times vary between 12.40pm and 3.05pm. An average school week lasts approximately 35 hours.
Attendance
It is important that all parents know that our school values high levels of attendance and punctuality. Regular school attendance and good timekeeping ensure that children have full access to the National Curriculum, Kodesh and all areas of school life. Full attendance at school also means that your child won’t fall behind. Just one session, one half day, one full day will put a pupil behind their classmates.
The school’s Attendance and Punctuality Policy is attached here for further information and detail.
Pupil Absence Requests – policy and form
If there is a valid reason you wish your son(s) to be absent from school, please complete the form found at this link: https://forms.gle/MMR78a4xTTp54K1Q6. The form must be completed and submitted for approval from the Headteacher. Without a formal request, the absence (apart from being unwell) will be recorded as unauthorised. Forms should be submitted preferably at least a week in advance. Forms submitted less than 48 hours before the absence is to be taken will not necessarily be authorised.
The school’s Attendance and Punctuality Policy is attached here for further information and detail.
Newsletters – weekly
Including both class newsletters and the weekly whole-school newsletter (posted on the school website – link below). These often colourful newsletters cover major aspects of the childrens’ learning during the school week, as well as highlighting any key pieces of information that parents may need to know. A key highlight of the weekly whole-school newsletter is the column of the Headteacher!
Click here to go to the newsletters page (password available on request from the school office)
Curriculum and Skills Information Sheets
Prepared by class teachers and sent out to parents at the beginning of each term, the sheets provide an outline of the topics and skills being taught in each subject that term. Also included is general information for parents regarding homework, PE etc.
The Curriculum and Skills Information Sheets can also be found in the Curriculum section of this website.
Annual Pupil Report – July
The annual report to parents is sent home in a sealed envelope before the end of the academic year. As well as reporting on pupil achievement, progress and effort in all academic subjects, the report also contains sections on individual pupil’s character as well as a general comments section and final comments from the Headteacher. Attendance is also reported, including any authorised and unauthorised absences.
‘Coffee and Cream Cakes with the Headteacher and Menahel’ – three times a year
This informal parents’ forum was initiated by the current Headteacher and takes place before the end of the Autumn, Spring and Summer terms. Parents are invited to join the Headteacher and Menahel over Danish pastries and hot drinks in the Boardroom, to share their thoughts, ideas and other comments and feedback regarding our school. Minutes are taken and then shared with the parent body.
Please click here for Minutes of the most recent meeting.
Parents in Class – once a year
Spread across several days, parents are invited to sign up for the opportunity to spend a lesson with their boys in their classrooms. A very popular initiative upon its inception last year, these sessions open parents’ eyes into what really takes place in school. Feedback forms are available at the end of the session. This feedback goes on to play a key part of our ongoing evaluation of lesson content and delivery.
Click here for a photo page!
Parents and Pupils Reading Together – twice a year
Spread across two days, parents are invited to come into school and spend some quality time reading with their boys. Different sessions are timed for each year group in the school.
Click here for a photo page!
Parents Evenings – Autumn and Spring terms
Parents are invited to meet with their child’s teacher to discuss their child’s academic progress and anything else of importance. The Headteacher is also in school during these evenings. Parents are allocated 7-minute slots with the teacher. If need be, another more extended meeting can be arranged. Morning appointments are also offered to parents.
* School prefects are on duty during these evenings to guide parents to the right classrooms, manage time for everyone and keep staff refreshed!
Curriculum Evenings – Autumn term
Held early on in the Autumn term, this is an opportunity for parents to come and hear from the Headteacher and Menahel about the school, how it is moving forwards and plans for the new academic year.
Parents have the opportunity to meet with their sons’ new class teachers and Rebbes, learn more about the academic curriculum and are invited to ask general questions of their teachers and Rebbes.
Sessions are held across different evenings as many of our parents have more than one child in the school and we wish to give them the opportunity to hear from and meet their sons’ teachers and Rebbes.
Parent Information Evenings and Workshops – throughout the year
Throughout the school year, various information evenings and workshops are held in the school on a wide range of topics e.g. ‘Preparing for Year 6 SATs’, ‘Reading With Your Children’, ‘Healthy Eating’, ‘Helping Your Child With Their Homework’, ‘First Aid’, ‘Introduction to Phonics’, ‘Managing Relationships Between Boys’ and more. Most of these sessions are led by school staff and occasionally by outside facilitators for example from the Local Authority. Parents are invited to by letter to these evenings and while asked to inform the school beforehand of their attendance, are still welcome to join us on the night.
Assemblies – weekly
Parents are invited to attend assemblies when their children’s class is performing. They are given due notice of the dates in the termly calendars. Parents of pupils in Year 6 are also invited to attend assembly when their son is reading the weekly D’var Torah (short speech on the weekly Torah portion).
Performance Assemblies – Autumn & Summer terms
Children playing a musical instrument or talented at singing are given the chance to perform in two special concerts in the Autumn and Summer terms. These concerts take place in front of all pupils and in front of parents of performing artists.
Click here for a photo page!
Sports Day – Summer term
Taking place in the summer term at the Stone X, Barnet Copthall Stadium, this is one of the highlights of the school calendar. All children from Reception to Year 6 take part in a host of activities from team races to individual track and field activities. Parents are invited to attend, watch, cheer and support their boys.
Click here for photo page of Sports Day!
Mothers @ Pardes (M@P)
This group of school mothers are responsible for the planning and organisation of the school’s monthly Rosh Chodesh activities, Chumash Seudah, Year 6 Graduation celebrations and much more besides. The group meets with the Headteacher and Menahel regarding the planning and coordination of these various events and activities, all of which are enjoyed tremendously by our hard-working pupils. M@P welcome additional help and support from other like-minded parents.

Grandparents Day – every two years
Grandparents are very proud of their grandchildren. So why not invite them into the school for one special day a year just for them? Even great-grandparents are welcome too!
In the Spring term an on a bi-annual basis, grandparents are invited to spend a morning or afternoon in school with their grandsons; joining them in classrooms, taking them out to read with them in the comfort of our lovely Library and do other activities with them. Grandparents also have the opportunity to sit and chat with the Headteacher and Menahel over tea, coffee and delicious cream cakes. An opportunity not to be missed (and with over 120 grandparents attending in 2024!).
Click here for photo page!
Bikur Cholim ‘Pupil Support Team
An initiative first introduced as part of his election campaign by one of the members of the School Council, 2023-24. If your child is at home unwell, it won’t just be the parents being called to find out where their boys are or how they are doing. Our Bikur Cholim ‘Pupil Support Team’ will also be calling, if your child has been off school unwell for at least 48 hours.

pageCache.pageTitle: Beyond the curriculum | Pardes House Primary School
pageCache.text:
Cultural Capital
While at Pardes House, our pupils accumulate cultural capital by being exposed to the vital background knowledge and range of cultural experiences required to become active, informed, thoughtful citizens. Pupils benefit from the great opportunities that living in London offers, including access to museums, galleries, and exhibitions. Special visitors to the school enhance this still further for any and all year groups. Assemblies are often themed around national events and figures, both present and past. In addition to the formal curriculum, there are also special days and special weeks to enhance pupils’ school experience, while developing further important skills and depth of knowledge about their lives in school, outside school and beyond school.
All these wider opportunities for pupils are aligned with our ethos and mission so we can prepare our pupils for their journey through secondary school and beyond. To get the full picture, click here to see our extensive Cultural Capital map.
Educational visits and visitors
Our school believes very much in the importance of enhancing our pupils’ school experience through outings to places of interest in our rich and diverse capital city, as well as visitors and workshops in school. Parents are often invited to make a voluntary contribution towards the cost of these visits and the parents association also helps to fund the cost of outings and curriculum-linked school workshops. In Year 6, the children participate in a residential trip in addition to other special post-SATs outings and undergoing Safe Cycling Training.
To get the full picture: Click here to see our Outings / Innings Opportunities Map for the 2024-25 school year.
The Pardes House annual ‘Pause Day’
This annual event, started in 2023, takes the whole school off curriculum for the day. We switch from curriculum subjects to a day of active learning, personal development, creativity and other skills in a more fun, relaxed way. Click here to see what this looks like in our school.

pageCache.pageTitle: The 144 Club | Pardes House Primary School
pageCache.text:
The 144 Club is an initiative launched by the school at the start of the Spring term 2023. It was introduced to help boost the presence of Maths in the school and to help boys with their times tables development and knowledge. We have really seen how well this has worked and helped our boys!
“Knowing the times tables fluently helps children to develop their learning in maths because they can take that knowledge for granted, which frees up cognitive space for them to learn new mathematical ideas and apply maths to solve problems.”(Jo Boaler, Professor of Mathematics).
At Pardes House, we give all boys from Years 2 – 6 the opportunity to become a member of the 144 Club, through different levels. However, only those with full mastery of all their tables can be declared as 144 Club Masters! Some boys are so good at their tables that they are now sitting the ‘Ultra Master’ assessment!
Even the parents can see the benefit…
For more information on the club, click on the various links below.

STEM Science Club Mission Statement
The mission of the STEM Science Club in our school is to inspire curiosity, creativity, and critical thinking through hands-on exploration and discovery in the fields of Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics.
Our goal is to provide a collaborative environment where the boys can engage in fun, interactive learning experiences that foster a deeper understanding of the world around them.
Through participation in the club, our boys develop essential skills such as problem-solving, teamwork, and innovation, while expanding their knowledge in key STEM concepts. By encouraging experimentation and exploration, we aim to empower our 40+ club members to become future leaders in science and technology, equipped with the confidence and skills to tackle challenges and contribute to a sustainable and exciting future.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral at Pardes | Pardes House Primary School
pageCache.text:
Rationale
Pardes House is committed to the well-being of all its pupils. As such, the school has a dedicated Pastoral Lead (Mrs B Davis), who plays a pivotal role in fostering a nurturing and inclusive environment. Mrs Davis’s work recognises the profound impact that emotional and social development can have on a pupil’s overall success.
From the very start of the school day, our Pastoral Leader is working with families, to make sure their boys are ready to come in, ready and happy to learn. One of our Pastoral Lead’s key responsibilities involves creating a safe space for pupils to express themselves openly and seek guidance when needed. Mrs Davis actively engages with pupils on a personal level, developing strong relationships built on trust and understanding. Mrs Davis’s approach addresses not only academic challenges but also the emotional and social aspects of each pupil. She is always ready to lend a listening ear and provide the support necessary for pupils to navigate the complexities of school life and growing up.
Qualifications
Mrs Davis has completed a number of training programs to aid her support for our boys, including TQUK Level 2 Core Counselling Skills, Emotional Literacy Support Assistant (ELSA), Place2Be Mental Health Champions, UK Child Bereavement and Designated Safeguarding Lead training.
Mrs Davis collaborates closely with parents, teachers, senior leaders and other staff to ensure a cohesive and comprehensive approach to pastoral care. Within her role, Mrs Davis leads and/or has arranged a number of school pastoral interventions…
Pastoral Interventions at Pardes
All of this work contributes to the overall well-being of the school community. Mrs Davis dedicates herself to the pastoral care aspect of education, which plays a vital role in creating an environment where pupils not only thrive academically but also develop the skills and resilience needed for a successful and fulfilling life beyond the classroom.
